match.reason: The bank point covers competition policy and the laws that restrain firms, not the perfect competition market model with many small buyers and sellers, identical products and no price control, so it teaches a different idea.

draft.title: Perfect competition
card: Perfect competition is a model of a market. It is a standard to compare real markets against, and very few real markets match it fully.
It has four features: many small buyers and sellers, identical products, full information, and free entry and exit. Full information means buyers and sellers know the prices and quality on offer.
Each seller is so small that changing its output does not move the market price. Each buyer is also too small to move it.
So no one controls the price. Sellers are price takers: they accept the market price. If a seller charged more, buyers would switch to an identical product at the market price.
draft.remember: Many small sellers with identical products means no one controls the price.

a.q: Why can a single seller in a perfectly competitive market not set its own price?
opts: Buyers could buy an identical product at the market price
Sellers must follow a price set by the government
Buyers are all large enough to bargain over the price
New sellers cannot enter, so prices stay fixed
a.why: Products are identical and there are many sellers, so a seller that charged more would lose its buyers to others at the market price. The model does not rely on the government setting prices, and entry is free.
a.clue: Think about where a buyer could go if one seller charged more.

b.q: Wheat farmers in Victoria sell the same grade of wheat to many buyers. Everyone knows the going price, and any farmer can start or stop growing it. Farmer Ana raises her price 10% above the going price. What is most likely to happen?
opts: She sells almost none, as buyers use other farmers
She sells the same amount, as her farm is well known
She sells less, but the market price rises by 10%
She sells the same amount, as buyers dislike switching
b.why: The wheat is identical and buyers know the going price, so they can buy from other farmers at no extra cost. Ana is one small seller, so she is a price taker and cannot move the market price. Her brand being well known does not matter when the product is identical.
b.clue: Ana's wheat is the same as everyone else's, and buyers know the price.

a.best: Buyers could buy an identical product at the market price

b.best: She sells almost none, as buyers use other farmers
